### Summary

One Runge-Kutta stage of a block is a fixed schedule of named ops, built once per block by its stage executor
({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::build_schedule >}}): the stage-entry ghost exchange (a bare block
only), `advance` (the hydro and scalar increments), `forcing`[^rg-72eb2816da59] (the user callbacks), `combine` (the integrator's average
with the step-start state), and the end-of-stage slots `saturation`, `chemistry` and `boundaries`. The executor runs
the schedule eagerly, or groups the ops into segments and replays each capturable segment as a CUDA graph
({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::run_stage >}}); either way the ops are the same. This section
follows that schedule and writes out the three small identities the combination and the tracer transfer rest on,
because later chapters cite them. Capture, the segments and the refusal list are @sec-ch13-cuts and @sec-ch13-agree; the capture sweep is
@sec-ch16-capture.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Combine a stage (@eq-ch01-stage-combine, @eq-ch01-stage-weight); carry tracers (@eq-ch01-stage-dry).

**Data.** In: `hydro_u`, `scalar_s`, the stage weights, any user increments. Out: the combined interior state.

**Placement.** Once per RK stage: the schedule's ops `advance`, `forcing` and combine (`stage_combine`), between the exchange and `boundaries`.

**Activation.** User increments only with callbacks installed (`user_stage_forcings`); the stages are pyharp's.

**Guarantee / limits.** The combine is an affine recurrence in the weights, exact in arithmetic; no spatial order.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch01-stage-tests; `test_stage_schedule.<b>`, `test_mesh_executor.<b>`, `test_user_output.<b>`, `stage_check.py` `[C1]`-`[C4]`.
:::
Local symbols: $J^{\mathrm{d}}_{i+1/2}$ is the already time-integrated implicit dry-air transfer through a face
[$\mathrm{kg}$], positive toward increasing $x_1$; $J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}$ is its upwind passive-tracer
transfer [$\mathrm{kg}$]. Here $n$ labels a passive tracer and $r_n$ is its ratio per unit dry mass.
Superscripts $\mathrm{carry}$ and $\mathrm{source}$ mark the selected carry ratio and a source increment.
These transfer symbols are defined locally above.

### Derivation

The fields in this section are cell averages. The conserved vector $\mathbf U$[^rg-879841a906d0] holds densities, momentum
densities and the energy density with the units of appendix A, and $\Delta t$ is the step [s].

Write $\Delta\mathbf U$ for the supplied stage increment, in the units of the corresponding conserved
component. The source comment states the combine as an in-place affine recurrence with the weights
$w_0^{(s)}, w_1^{(s)}, w_2^{(s)}$ of stage $s$:

$$
\mathbf U \leftarrow w_0^{(s)}\mathbf U^n + w_1^{(s)}\mathbf U + w_2^{(s)}\Delta\mathbf U.
$$ {#eq-ch01-stage-combine}

@eq-ch01-stage-combine is the call `pintg->forward(stage, u0, u, du, u)` of the combine op (`stage_combine`)
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_combine >}}); the weights are the integrator's
(pyharp's) stage weights. The increment here includes whichever explicit and implicit operations were selected, not
only the explicit increment $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$[^rg-e6248a941ab9] of appendix A.

Consider a fixed supplied increment in stage $s$, holding the later increments fixed. It enters the combination
with the coefficient $w_2^{(s)}$. The next combine multiplies this contribution by $w_1^{(s+1)}$, and the saved
step-start state contributes no copy of it. Repeating the substitution through each later stage gives the
final coefficient

$$
w_2^{(s)}\prod_{s'>s}w_1^{(s')}.
$$ {#eq-ch01-stage-weight}

@eq-ch01-stage-weight is the weight with which the flux register's step sum holds a stage's face fluxes: the
register applies the same recurrence to its sums, $S \leftarrow w_1^{(s)} S + w_2^{(s)}\Delta t\,T^{(s)}$ for the
stage's flux total $T^{(s)}$ ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::end_stage >}}), so after the last stage
$T^{(s)}$ enters $S$ with @eq-ch01-stage-weight times $\Delta t$. The product runs over the remaining stages and an empty
product is one. The identity is exact for the bookkeeping of supplied increments; it is not a linearization of their
state dependence. The weights are pyharp's, so this chapter does not assert their values from a snapy call site. Check `[C1]` expands a generic three-stage affine recurrence
symbolically [check `src/snapy_report/ch01/checks/stage_check.py`, output `stage_check.out`].

The tracer transfer and its dry-source complement are derived in @sec-ch08-drycarry; this section keeps the call
interface, the three identities the code evaluates and the donor cap. Before the cap, the transfer of tracer $n$
through an $x_1$ face is the clamped dry transfer $J^{\mathrm{d}}$ of the implicit mass-correction buffer times the
ratio of the donor cell,

$$
J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2} = J^{\mathrm{d}}_{i+1/2}
\begin{cases}
r_{n,i}, & J^{\mathrm{d}}_{i+1/2}>0,\\
r_{n,i+1}, & J^{\mathrm{d}}_{i+1/2}\le 0,
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ch01-stage-upwind}

the upwind tensor `P` of {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_advance >}}. Each transfer is then
capped by what its donor holds, the `donor_cap` sweep ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_dispatch.cpp donor_cap_cpu >}},
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_dispatch.cu donor_cap_cuda >}}). Let $H_{n,i}$ [kg] be the tracer mass cell $i$ holds
after the stage's explicit update, $V_i(\rho_{\mathrm d}r_n)_i$ with a negative value counted as zero. Up one column, from
the lowest interior cell $i_l$:

1. *Start.* $A_{i_l}=H_{n,i_l}$, what the lowest cell can give.
2. *Clamp the face above cell $i$.* $J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}\leftarrow\min\big(\max(J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2},-H_{n,i+1}),\,A_i\big)$:
   an upward transfer takes at most $A_i$, a downward one at most what cell $i+1$ holds.
3. *Carry up.* $A_{i+1}=H_{n,i+1}+J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}$: what cell $i+1$ holds plus what entered it from below,
   never negative because of step 2.
4. *No cell goes negative.* Cell $i$ ends with $H_{n,i}+J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i-1/2}-J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}=A_i-J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}$.
   An upward $J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}$ is at most $A_i$, and a downward one adds mass, so the result is $\ge0$.
5. *Conservation.* Each face value is used by both of its cells, so the column total is unchanged.
6. *A uniform ratio is untouched.* The VIC[^rg-828441330efe] clamps the dry transfer by the same rule (@sec-ch09-vic-redistribute).
   With one ratio $r_n$ everywhere, $J^{\mathrm{tr}}=r_nJ^{\mathrm{d}}$ and $H_n=r_nH_{\mathrm d}$, so every tracer bound is
   $r_n$ times a dry bound the dry transfer already meets, and the cap does not bind (the `through` test measures it).

The CPU first tests every face against $H_{n,i}$ plus the unclamped inflow and runs the sweep only if one binds,
which gives the same result; CUDA runs the sweep in one thread per column with no host read. Check `[C4]` ports the
sweep. The increment of a cell is the net capped transfer over its volume $V_i$[^rg-902e93eb3066] [$\mathrm{m^3}$],

$$
\Delta\rho_{n,i} = \frac{J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i-1/2}-J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}}{V_i},
$$ {#eq-ch01-stage-transfer}

the `P - P_above` update of the same function; and a supplied dry-mass source carries the tracers at the
selected carry ratio $r^{\mathrm{carry}}_n$,

$$
\Delta\rho^{\mathrm{source}}_n = r^{\mathrm{carry}}_n\,\Delta\rho^{\mathrm{source}}_{\mathrm{d}},
$$ {#eq-ch01-stage-dry}

`carry_dry_source` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::carry_dry_source >}}). Checks
`[C2]` and `[C3]` exercise the two identities on a port, with the committed output `stage_check.out`; they
import no snapy.

### Numerical method

The `advance` op, `stage_advance` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_advance >}}), first
publishes the stage to the hydro module. On stage zero it starts the flux register's step, runs the step-start half of
every split source and refills and exchanges the ghosts if one exists, and saves the step-start state (`u0`, `s0` in the
state store); the split source at the pin is the radial conduction of `implicit_radial`[^rg-4ddc775769de] diffusion on the cubed
sphere (@sec-ch07-csdiffusion). It then opens the register's stage and takes the hydro increment (@sec-ch01-hydro),
time-integrated, and the scalar increment (@sec-ch01-scalar), which uses the hydro dry-mass flux and the implicit dry
transfer; native dry sources carry the tracers after the transfer. The `forcing` op,
`stage_forcing` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_forcing >}}), applies the user callbacks
in list order; user dry sources carry the tracers after all callbacks, from the saved pre-callback scalar increment, and
a callback result may contain only `hydro_du` and `scalar_ds`, with matching shapes. The combine op,
`stage_combine` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_combine >}}), closes the register's stage,
averages with the integrator, runs the second half of every split source after the last stage's average, applies the
conserved limiter and refills the solid cells (@sec-ch14-solids). On the last stage `saturation` runs the saturation
adjustment on the interior cells when a thermodynamics module and a nonempty reaction list exist (@sec-ch08-satadj), and
`chemistry` runs a registered chemistry step, on a bare block and on a Mesh's block alike (@sec-ch01-mesh). `boundaries` fills the
physical ghosts last (@sec-ch14-timing). The tendencies are block storage, so `forcing` and the combine op read them across a
segment boundary. This map asserts algebraic identities, not an observed convergence order.

The schedule groups consecutive ops of the same kind and capturability into segments; the stage-entry exchange is a
segment of its own, and an op that cannot be captured runs eagerly with its reason recorded
({{< code src/mesh/segment.cpp StageSchedule::add >}}). At the pin three ops can turn eager: `forcing` when a user
TorchScript forcing is set, `chemistry` when a chemistry step is registered, and `boundaries` when an outflow face is
set ({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::build_schedule >}}).

@fig-ch01-stage-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}

#| fig-cap: "Accumulate and combine one stage. Labelled green boxes name operations or owners; black arrows show the reading sequence, not a timing measurement."
#| fig-alt: "Sequence: exchange (bare block); publish stage / save; hydro increment; scalar / dry carry; user increments; RK / limiter / solids; last-stage saturation, chemistry / BC."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_stage_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why the combine is exact up to a bounded round-off.** Fix one cell and one row. The combine evaluates
$w_0\mathbf U^n + w_1\mathbf U + w_2\Delta\mathbf U$ with three products and two sums, five roundings in all, each
with relative error at most $\delta_{\mathrm{mach}} = 2^{-53}$. Dropping products of two rounding errors, the computed
value differs from the exact one by at most
$5\,\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}\,(|w_0\mathbf U^n| + |w_1\mathbf U| + |w_2\Delta\mathbf U|)$; the recurrence of
@eq-ch01-stage-weight inherits one such bound per stage. The transfer update of @eq-ch01-stage-transfer is three
operations per cell ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_advance >}}). They are the product $r_n M$
that forms each face transfer `P`, the subtraction `P - P_above`, and the division by the cell volume. Each product
rounds once, so the two transfers carry an absolute error of at most
$\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}(|J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i-1/2}| + |J^{\mathrm{tr}}_{n,i+1/2}|)$ into the difference. The
subtraction itself is exact only when the two transfers have the same sign and lie within a factor of two of each
other. Otherwise it rounds once more, by at most $\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}$ of the difference. The division adds one
rounding of the result. When the two transfers nearly cancel, the product errors are not small relative to the result.
A capped transfer is a bound instead of the product: $A_i$ is one addition, one rounding, and the clamps themselves
are exact.

: Implementation anchors for one stage. {#tbl-ch01-stage-code}

1. Build the schedule and run it: `build_schedule` and `run_stage`
   ({{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::build_schedule >}},
   {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::run_stage >}}).
2. Publish the stage, save the step-start state, take the hydro and scalar increments, carry the tracers with the dry
   transfer (`mass_corr`) and the native dry sources: `stage_advance`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_advance >}}).
3. Apply the user callbacks: `stage_forcing` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_forcing >}}).
4. Close the register's stage, combine with `pintg`, refill solids: `stage_combine`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_combine >}}); on the last stage adjust saturation and run a
   bare block's chemistry; fill the physical ghosts
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_boundaries >}}).
5. The weight of a stage's increment in the step sum: `end_stage`
   ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::end_stage >}}).

**How to use it.** User increments are installed as scripted modules, one file per callback, in list order:

```cpp
mesh->set_user_stage_forcings({"heating.pt", "drag.pt"});
```

Each module receives the stage inputs, $\Delta t$ and the stage index, and returns a dictionary. It may contain
only `hydro_du` and `scalar_ds`, with the shapes of `hydro_u` and `scalar_s`. Any other key or shape is
refused ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_advance.cpp MeshBlockImpl::stage_forcing >}}). The recurrence behind
@eq-ch01-stage-weight is these lines of `FluxRegister::end_stage`
({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.cpp FluxRegister::end_stage >}}):

```cpp
auto w2dt = dt.scaled(_w2);  // V3 D: on the device in a captured stage
for (int d = 0; d < 3; ++d) {
  if (!_step[d].defined()) continue;
  // in FP64 (FP32 on MPS), whatever the flux dtype: S <- w1 S + w2 dt T
  if (!_direct[d].defined()) {
    axpy_(_step[d].mul_(_w1), _total[d].to(_step[d].scalar_type()), w2dt);
    continue;
  }
```

Each stage multiplies the sum by $w_1$ and adds $w_2\Delta t$ times the stage's total, so unrolling over the remaining stages gives the two factors of @eq-ch01-stage-weight.

: Source assertions for the stage. {#tbl-ch01-stage-tests}

The assertions are {{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserForcing.scripted_stage_forcings_add_tendencies_in_list_order >}},
{{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserForcing.scripted_module_is_shared_across_parallel_blocks >}},
{{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserForcing.scripted_stage_forcing_rejects_unsupported_keys >}} and
`main` of {{< code tests/test_jit_user_forcing.py main >}}.

The check is symbolic and numeric, with no snapy import.[^ch01-stage-run] `[C1]`: the supplied-stage
coefficients of a generic three-stage recurrence equal @eq-ch01-stage-weight, residuals 0. `[C2]`: the
upwind transfer telescopes over closed and open ends with residual 0 against a tolerance of
$1.4\times10^{-14}$. `[C3]`: the dry-source carry matches @eq-ch01-stage-dry on both branches, symbolic residual 0. `[C4]`: on
2000 random columns of 12 cells, all of which the cap binds, no cell ends below zero, the column changes by at most
$4.34\times10^{-16}$ relative, the CPU pre-test gives the sweep's result exactly, and a uniform ratio through a dry
transfer that obeys the same cap moves by at most $3.13\times10^{-16}$ relative.

The ctests run on CPU, one rank; `test_user_output.<b>` also runs the parallel-block case in one process. At the pin
all of them passed on both builds:[^ch01-stage-ctest] `test_stage_schedule.release` and `test_user_output.release`
with all cases run (5 and 29), `test_mesh_executor.release` with 4 of 8 cases on CPU (the CUDA cases skip there) and
all 8 on CUDA, and the Python callback and donor-cap tests. `donor` printed a minimum tracer density of $0$ and a total
change of $0$; `through` a ratio change of $6.66\times10^{-16}$ with $1.433$ cell masses moved through a cell; the
upper-bound case a minimum of $0$; the two builds printed the same numbers.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The stage algebra proves neither positivity after arbitrary user increments nor accuracy after nonlinear
limiting or phase adjustment. The donor cap keeps the implicit tracer transfer from overdrawing a donor; where it
binds, the tracer no longer moves with the ratio of the dry transfer, so a non-uniform ratio is changed there
(first order, donor-limited). Switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix; the runs above are one CPU
build and one CUDA device, one rank each.
:::

[^rg-e6248a941ab9]: $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$ — the explicit stage increment handed to the implicit solve

[^rg-828441330efe]: VIC — vertically implicit correction

[^rg-902e93eb3066]: $V_i$ — cell volume

[^rg-4ddc775769de]: implicit_radial — whether radial heat conduction on the cubed sphere is solved implicitly, split around the explicit step (default false)

[^rg-0ed3cc23ed9a]: upper-bound — upper bound for the scalar ratio; a negative value disables the bound
